body:
Found while finishing #1442, not reported by a user.

`fb3c7e4c8` removed the startup `dependency_check()` loop from `cps/__init__.py`.
Before it, a required package that was absent produced:

    *** Cannot import tabulate module, it is needed to run calibre-web,
        please install it using "pip install tabulate" ***

and `sys.exit(8)`. The rationale for removing it is sound and I agreed with it:
it duplicated pip's resolver, and `dep_version_int` got the comparison wrong
anyway (`int(x) if x.isnumeric() else 0` collapsed `2.0.0rc1` to `(2,0,0)`).

The gap it leaves is narrow but real. OBSERVED on `:v4.1.32` with `tabulate`
uninstalled: the container restart-loops and the only diagnostic is

    File "/app/calibre-web-automated/scripts/cwa_db.py", line 14
    from tabulate import tabulate
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tabulate'

Docker users cannot hit this — the image installs from pyproject at build time.
It reaches source installs that pull new code into an existing venv without
re-running `pip install`, where a newly declared dependency is simply absent.
The traceback does name the module, so it is diagnosable rather than silent;
it is just a worse first-run experience than the old message.

Not fixed in #1442 because that PR's scope was the About-page half, and the
lazily-imported case (the one where the app boots and the failure IS invisible)
is now covered by the marker fix + un-suppressed `not installed` rows.

If this is worth closing, the cheap version is a guarded import at the entry
point that catches ImportError and re-raises with the install hint, rather than
reinstating a version-comparing check.
title: A missing startup-critical dependency now fails with a raw traceback instead of a named install instruction
